title: Mailbox and relay federation routes sign HTTP 500, not a signed UNKNOWN 503, when the receiver fails to collect a response body
outcome: When the receiver fails to collect a response body on a mailbox or mailbox-relay route, the sender gets a signed UNKNOWN reply. That reply is classified as "outcome may be unknown" (503 class) for the mailbox operation, never as a definite failure, and it never fences. This matches the smaller-limit routes.
acceptance: On mailbox and mailbox-relay routes, a handler response whose body stream fails or overflows is signed as an UNKNOWN outcome. It uses the same signed 503 envelope as the smaller-limit routes and keeps each route's existing typed mailbox envelope where one applies. Both route limits are preserved: the 64 MiB finite-output bound and the route's own response limit. Shown by a behavioural test that drives the mailbox branch, as well as the health branch, with a failing and an overflowing body.
The sender's mailbox classification of that reply is UNKNOWN, with the idempotency key retained, and the link is kept. No timeout or limit value changes.
The review pair has no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding, and the full gate passes on the exact landed input.
